text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- A German criminal court accuses Turkish government of protecting international drugs trade.
- Government MP in security scandal says silencers found in back of car he was travelling in probably belonged to a fellow passenger, late gangster Abdullah Catli.
- Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan gearing up to give an ultimatom to Greece on planned Greek Cypriot deployment of S-300 anti-aircraft missiles.
- Military is angered by call for greater democracy by leading business organisation.
- Turkish navy force will arrive in Cyprus on January 24.
- Sixteen youths who were tortured in police custody last year were allegedly questioned by a repentant Kurdish rebel.
- General manager of private Egebank says the number of banks is low in Turkey.
- Parliamentary commission investigating a security scandal not satistfied with testimony government MP.
